item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Aug 18, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Aug 20, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: First Annual Connectivity Day — Sat Sep 12, 12:00 PM — 204 Spring Garden Street
item.description:
The Anne Brossman Sweigart Charitable Foundation will host its first annual community fundraiser, “Connectivity Day“. The afternoon invites neighbors to a rare visit inside one of Ephrata’s landmark homes, with every dollar raised benefiting Ephrata Area Social Services (EASS).
Guests will enjoy local food trucks, live music, guided tours of the historic house, and a raffle. The afternoon opens with a VIP hour from 11:30 to 12:30 p.m., welcomes the general public from 1:00 to 3:00 p.m., and closes from 3:00 to 4:00 p.m. with a special reunion honoring retirees of the Denver & Ephrata (D&E) Telephone Company. Admission is $10, with 100% of the proceeds benefitting EASS. Space is limited, and advance purchase is required.
Get tickets
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Lancaster MusicFest — Sat Sep 12, 12:00 PM — Buchanan Park
item.description:
Bring your crew, your blanket, and your appetite. On September 12, Buchanan Park turns into Lancaster’s favorite outdoor party as the SmartHub Foundation presents the 7th annual Lancaster MusicFest, a full day of live music, local food, and good company under the open sky.
Sip local craft beer, wine, and spirits. Grab a bite from Lancaster’s best food vendors. Catch street performers, shop handmade goods from local artisans, and settle into open green space with friends and family. It’s music, community, and Lancaster County all in one place. Every ticket supports two causes close to home: Children’s Miracle Network and Schreiber Pediatric. Since day one, MusicFest has existed to amplify the local organizations making Lancaster more engaged, healthier, and more vibrant. Come for the music. Stay for the community. This is Lancaster at its best.
Learn More
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Aug 19, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
